sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, status, reason, manager_id, reviewed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of all leave requests for a given employee; status: filtering by pending/approved/rejected status for manager dashboards; leave_type: filtering by annual/sick/emergency for balance calculations and reporting; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for overlapping leave detection and calendar views; manager_id: lookups of requests awaiting a specific manager's review

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, year, total_days, used_days, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id, leave_type, year: unique constraint and primary lookup for a specific employee's balance for a given leave type and year; employee_id: balance lookups scoped to an employee; leave_type: aggregate balance queries across employees by type

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, actor_id, changes, created_at | pk: id | fks: actor_id -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: lookups of all audit records for a specific entity; actor_id: audit trail filtered by the acting user; created_at: time-range audit queries

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type, days_per_year, max_consecutive_days, requires_approval, allow_negative_balance, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: unique lookup of the active policy for a given leave type; is_active: filtering active policies

findByManagerId(managerId: string, filters?: { status?: LeaveStatus }): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
findOverlapping(employeeId: string, startDate: Date, endDate: Date, excludeId?: string): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
updateStatus(id: string, status: LeaveStatus, managerId: string, reviewedAt: Date, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest>
findByEmployeeTypeYear(employeeId: string, leaveType: LeaveType, year: number): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>
upsertBalance(employeeId: string, leaveType: LeaveType, year: number, totalDays: number, usedDays: number, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance>
incrementUsedDays(employeeId: string, leaveType: LeaveType, year: number, days: number, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance>

data_notes: The employees table is referenced via FK from leave_requests and leave_balances but is owned by the existing employee module — not defined here. The audit_logs table is defined here per GP-002; every state-changing operation (create leave request, approve/reject) writes an audit record. The leave_policies table holds the configurable rules per leave type (annual, sick, emergency) that drive balance calculations and validation. leave_balances uses a composite unique constraint on (employee_id, leave_type, year) enforced at the application/repository layer; the code agent should add a DB-level unique index for this.

open_questions.question: How are leave balances seeded for a new year — are they pre-inserted by a scheduled job at year start, or computed on-the-fly as (policy.days_per_year - SUM(approved leave days))?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether leave_balances rows are always present or may be absent for an employee-year-type combination, which changes the repository's upsert vs. read-then-compute semantics and the service-layer logic for balance checks.
candidate_options: Pre-seed via scheduled job at year start for all active employees
Compute on-the-fly: balance = policy.days_per_year - SUM(approved days); leave_balances table becomes a cache or is removed
Hybrid: pre-seed with total_days from policy, then increment used_days on each approval

transaction_contract: Repository methods that participate in multi-step writes (create, updateStatus, upsertBalance, incrementUsedDays) accept an optional `client: PoolClient` parameter. When omitted, the method acquires its own connection from the shared pool for single-step operations. The calling service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, executes BEGIN, passes the client to each repository call in sequence, then executes COMMIT or ROLLBACK. This contract is essential for the approve/reject flow, which must atomically update leave_requests.status and leave_balances.used_days.
